Data notes

Heartopia doesn't publish an official item database, so the numbers here are gathered from community wikis and guides (linked in the footer). Quantities, prices and unlock conditions may be approximate or drift as the game updates — treat this as a helpful starting point, not gospel. Your tracker data (checklists, inventory, goals) is saved on this device only, in this browser — see the Tracker tab for backing it up, moving it to another device, or signing in with Google to sync it automatically.

Spot something wrong or missing? There's no live editing here, but you know the game better than any wiki — use the Tracker's custom entries to fill gaps for yourself.

Flowers

Grow times, seed costs and what each star rating sells for — plus how crossbreeding actually works.

FlowerLvSeedGrow time ★1★2★3★4★5
Selling seeds back. Albert buys seeds at half what you paid for them, so a 300g Rose seed returns 150g — worth knowing before you clear out a stack you over-bought.

Crossbreeding

Plant two flowers next to each other, water them, and they leave a seed of a new colour behind.

Colour is really a star rating. Every bloom sits at a star level, and a cross is resolved on those stars — not on the colours themselves. So nine 1-star white flowers side by side can still throw a 2-star pink or orange; what matters is the pair of star ratings going in.

What a pair produces

ParentParentResult

A lower rating can still turn up instead — these are the intended results, not a guarantee.

Getting it to happen

  1. Plant alternately. Set the two parents in a checkerboard so each one has the other as a neighbour.
  2. Water them. Watering is what drives the cross along.
  3. Collect the seed that appears — that's your new colour.

Watering tops out at 5 levels a day, shown in game as the number of sparkles over the plant — one sparkle for level 1 up to five at the cap. Past that, more watering does nothing until tomorrow.

Matching the two parents' star ratings raises your odds. Pairing a low rating with a high one tends to drag the result down toward the lower parent.

Quests & progression systems

How tasks and quests are organized, from what could be pieced together.

About "D.G." — per AthenaMM's community sheet, D.G. is a 70+ level membership track that advances through Contribution Medals earned by completing resident quests (0 medals at Level 1, up to 600 at Level 70). It gates fishing/gardening/building basics early on, then painting, dreams, music recording, new locations (Whale Fall Canyon, Island Terminal), warehouse space and pickaxe durability later, and hands out Premium Hobby Upgrade Tickets, recipes, building permits and cosmetic profile items along the way. What the initials literally stand for still isn't documented publicly in the sources we could find.

Shop prices

What the shopkeepers charge for ingredients you can't grow or gather.

This is where recipe costs come from. A dish's Cost is its ingredients added up at base price, counting seed cost for anything you grow yourself. Every recipe whose ingredients are all listed here works out to exactly the cost shown in the Recipes tab, so the two sets of numbers agree. In the Recipes tab, hover a cost to see the sum it's made of.
Prices that aren't printed in any shop▸
Some ingredients never appear on a shop list. Their prices were worked back out of the recipes instead: take a dish whose cost is known and which has only one unpriced ingredient, and that ingredient's price falls out of the arithmetic. Each one was then re-checked against every other recipe using it, and 113 of the 154 recipes now reconcile to the penny. Everything foraged or fished came out at 0g, which is what the "all foraged" dishes already implied. The ones that cost something: Vegetable and Wakame 10g, Sea Grape 18g, Tomato Sauce 40g (its own four tomatoes), White Daisy 60g, Red Rose 300g.

Cooking recipes

Ingredients, cost, and sell price by recipe — pick a star level per category. Full star-by-star profit is in Calculators → Cooking profit.

Where the regular recipe data comes from▸
Levels, ingredients and gold figures in the regular categories were transcribed from a player-made spreadsheet, then checked line by line — including the Seafood and Sets sections — against AthenaMM's community-maintained price sheet, which caught one missing ingredient (Smoked Fish Bagel's Vegetable). Every cell here is read-only; the Cooking profit calculator is the place to explore star levels interactively.
Event recipes are community-sourced▸
Echo of Ancients is fully confirmed via AthenaMM's price sheet — ingredients, costs, gold prices and Fashion Token prices — and the fish, insects, birds, crops and store items from that same event are gathered in Wiki → Live event. Call of Whales, Winter Frost Season, Dreamlight Cinematics and Modular Streets Festival come from public community wikis and guides only — ingredient quantities there are sometimes approximate, and several dishes have no confirmed sell price yet (shown as "—"). A few other known event dishes, such as Qixi Fair's Qiaoguo, aren't listed at all because no reliable ingredient list could be found.

Weather forecast

Heartopia's weather follows a fixed calendar, so it can be read ahead. Several fish, insects and ores only appear under one condition.

What the icons mean

Each day is split into the game's four 6-hour windows: Dawn 00–06, Morning 06–12, Afternoon 12–18, Evening 18–24. Dates follow the real calendar.

Forecast data by Th.gl. The weather calendar is compiled by Th.gl's Heartopia weather forecast, and is reproduced here with credit. This page is a separate reading of that data, not a copy of their tool — for the authoritative calendar, the hour-by-hour detail and the meteor/aurora variant numbers, go to the source.

Cooking profit ranking

Every dish's net profit at the star level you pick, versus the value of just selling the raw ingredients.

RecipeLevelCostSell priceNet profitRaw valueVerdict

"Raw value" is roughly what the uncooked ingredients would fetch on their own — when net profit doesn't clear it by much, cooking may not be worth the wait.

Recipes with an unconfirmed sell price (mostly newer event dishes) are listed in the Recipes tab but left out of this ranking.

A cost of 0g* means every ingredient is foraged or fished — nothing to buy, so the whole sell price is profit. It costs gathering time instead of gold, which is why those dishes rank so high here.
